label: Logistic model: the predicted probability that patient i has the event, given the score s(i) built from the centered age u(i)
tex: \hat p_i = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-s_i}}, \qquad s_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 u_i + \cdots + \beta_d u_i^{d}, \;\; u_i = \frac{x_i - 50}{10}

label: Mean log loss: the average negative log-likelihood of the fit's probabilities on a data set
Area under the ROC curve: the probability that the model gives a higher score to a random event patient than to a random non-event patient
The overfitting gap: the difference between held-out and training log loss
Relative sample richness: the number of training rows per fitted coefficient, n divided by d plus one
